llm.summary: This skill has a coherent planning purpose, but it under-discloses network installs, model downloads, broad triggers, persistent template writes, and historical memory processing.

dimensions.detail: permissions.md declares no network, subprocess, deletion, or sensitive data access, but scripts and references show pip subprocesses, external model downloads, model directory replacement, arbitrary JSON path handling, and memory-log processing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifacts include pip-based dependency installation and Hugging Face/model-mirror downloads without pinned versions, revisions, or hashes; setup_env.py also appears syntactically broken, but the intended install behavior is still documented.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Triggers include broad everyday phrases such as general help and analysis requests, while the skill can run scripts and save templates; some references require user confirmation, but SKILL.md also describes automatic template saving.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Persistent capability/rule JSON files and model indexes are expected for the self-reinforcing template library, but historical-memory-derived templates and scheduled automation are not scoped with clear consent, redaction, retention, or deletion controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core semantic-splitting and JSON-template workflow fits the stated purpose, but the automation reference adds broad recent-memory log processing to generate persistent templates, which extends beyond current-task planning.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only in an isolated environment, avoid auto-install/model-download commands unless you accept the package and model supply-chain risk, do not allow it to scan agent memory without selecting exact files and redaction rules, and verify any generated JSON before it is saved or reused.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted in part: automation_tasks.md instructs reading recent memory logs and saving generalized capability JSON, which is broader than the declared no-data-access posture.
[T08] expected: Accepted as a supply-chain concern: dependency and model downloads support Pipeline A, but they are unpinned and not hash-verified.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: json_manager.py accepts user-supplied absolute or relative paths for several read/write commands, exceeding the declared data-directory boundary.
[other] unexpected: Accepted: permissions.md materially understates network, subprocess, deletion, filesystem, and memory behaviors found elsewhere in the artifact.
[TP4] expected: Partially accepted: model and package access is relevant to semantic matching and disclosed in some files, but it conflicts with the LOW/no-network permission declaration.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted: broad trigger phrases can activate this stateful planning skill in ordinary requests.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: progressive reference loading is disclosed and the referenced files were available for inspection.
[P6] expected: Not accepted: the cited 'rule' text refers to JSON rule generation, not system prompt disclosure.
[E2] expected: Downgraded: os.environ.copy appears tied to Hugging Face endpoint setup and no credential transmission was found, though the implementation is broader than necessary.
[SQP-2] expected: Accepted as a consent concern: persistent template saving is part of the skill design, but disclosure and opt-in behavior are inconsistent.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted: the docs contradict themselves by claiming no external/network activity while shipping install and model download workflows.
[RA2] expected: Downgraded: persistent JSON templates are expected data files, not a backdoor; the concern is scope and consent around scheduled generation and memory-derived content.
[SQP-3] expected: Not security-determinative: the skill is Chinese-language focused, but that does not itself show malicious behavior.
